domain: GLOBAL SEARCH (top-bar query → view 'search' results screen)
summary: Today the visible global search is 100% legacy demo. `AM.searchIndex` (309 entries) exists in italy-app-model.js but the string "searchIndex" appears ZERO times in portale.html — it is dead code. portale.html lines 3374-3385 build eight hardcoded groups by manually scanning D.CASES(29 decorated), A_SIGREAL(3, the only real source), D.PRODUCT_LIST(33), D.SCI_THEMES(10)+D.RECORDS(36), D.PEOPLE(39), D.COMPANIES(6), D.ARCHIVE(448) and D.SOURCES(53); each group caps display at 6 items while printing the full count. The markup (2355-2369) renders those groups and calls `i.go`, so every route target is decided inside the group builder. Facts come from the demo fixture even where a real equivalent exists: real portfolio is 166 products (163 regulatory + 3 catalog-only), not 33; real sources are 31, not 53; the real archive index is 740 rows across 7 kinds, not 448 manufactured rows. The searchTotal line also prints a hardcoded English sentence enumerating the eight groups, in an Italian-default product.
realSource: AM.searchIndex, rebuilt in italy-app-model.js over AM.collections: products(166) · windows(29, CANONICAL) · opportunities filtered to isUpstreamReal(3 of 29) · futureSignals(3) · voices(17) · researchers(60) · resistance(34) · scienceRecords(88) · themes(5, new) · sources(31) · channels(30) · events(18) · news(8) · marketObservations(77) · competitorActivities(503) · competitorCompanies(11 normalized, new) · competitorProducts(36, new). Measured target size 1114 entries vs 309 today, with ZERO cross-kind id collisions (verified). AM.archive is NOT indexed separately — it is already a derived index over science/market/competitor/voice/event/news/window, so indexing those kinds directly makes the ARCHIVE search group pure duplication.

modelChanges.why: The view must group and route with one reduce and one dispatcher, never a per-kind scan. Entry shape today lacks group, meta, routeArgs and provenance, which is precisely why portale.html hand-writes eight scans.
fields: group — UI group key the view buckets on: OPPORTUNITY | WINDOW | PRODUCT | SIGNAL | FIELD_VOICE | SCIENCE | PEOPLE | COMPETITOR | MARKET | SOURCE | NEWS | EVENT
id — the record's own id, in the namespace its destination view resolves
label — visible row text; never a concatenation containing a not-known note
meta — right-hand secondary text (ai, institution, platform, price unit, date)
routeArgs — extra state the dispatcher spreads (voiceId, sciFocusId, gireFocusId, mCrop, fCompany)
terms — lowercased, diacritic-folded, deduped, note-free, bilingually expanded
provenance — REAL_SOURCE | CANONICAL | REAL_DERIVED; DEMO_SCENARIO and SYNTHETIC_DEMO records are never pushed
modelChanges.derivation: One idx() call per collection over AM.collections. Sizes measured: product 166, window 29, opportunity 3 (isUpstreamReal only), signal 3, voice 17, researcher 60, resistance 34, science 88, theme 5, source 31, channel 30, event 18, news 8, market 77, competitorActivity 503, company 11, competitorProduct 36 = 1114 entries. Verified: no id collides across kinds.

Measured note contamination: voices.role 17/17, voices.organization 17/17, voices.region 17/17, researchers.role 60/60, futureSignals.region 2/3, resistance.speciesIt 1/34 and resistance.crop 1/34 plus 7/34 over 60 chars of prose.

issueTerms(raw) — raw + canonical i18n key + Italian label
modelChanges.derivation: cropTerms uses a measured alias table over the FIVE crop vocabularies actually present: canonical i18n keys in windows (Grapevine, Maize, Olive, Sugar Beet, Apple, Wheat, Durum Wheat, Tomato, Rice, Soybean); SCREAMING_SNAKE in voices/science (DURUM_WHEAT, VINE, MAIZE, OLIVE, CEREAL); Italian/Portuguese in news (MAIS, VITE, FRUMENTO, SOIA, ORTICOLE, CEREAIS); Latin binomials in competitor activities (Zea mays, Triticum aestivum, Vitis vinifera, Olea europaea, Solanum lycopersicum, Beta vulgaris, Malus domestica, Oryza sativa, Helianthus annuus, Citrus, Prunus persica) plus Italian generics (cereali, colture, frutta, ortaggi); and product crop codes (WHEAT_GENERIC, BARLEY, TRITICALE). Map ONLY the unambiguous pairs to an i18n key. CEREAL/CEREAIS/cereali/colture/frutta/ortaggi/ORTICOLE/Citrus/Prunus persica/WHEAT_GENERIC/BARLEY/TRITICALE have no unambiguous key and are indexed verbatim, never guessed. risks: Six of the twelve search groups (SOURCE, PEOPLE, COMPETITOR, EVENT, NEWS, and any science route through openTheme) land on screens that still resolve ids against the demo fixture with a `|| collection[0]` fallback. If the engineer wires them before those domains migrate, search becomes the fastest way in the whole product to reach a demo entity while believing it is real. The readiness gate is not optional polish — it is the safety mechanism for this change.

Search visibly gets emptier for some queries. Opportunity hits drop from 29 to 3; source hits from 53 to 31; researcher, source, company, event and news groups disappear entirely in phase 1. A reviewer who does not know the measurements will read this as a regression. Publish the before/after counts alongside the change.

The crop alias table is the one place in this spec where judgement enters the data path. Every entry must be a 1:1 lexical identity ('Zea mays' = 'Maize' = 'Mais'), never a semantic inference. 'CEREAL' → wheat, or 'cereali' → 'Frumento tenero', would be inventing a fact inside a lookup table, and it would be invisible in review because it lives in a synonym list rather than in a record.

Indexing all 503 competitor activities makes COMPETITOR the loudest group for almost any crop word (BASF alone has 138). With a 6-row cap and an honest '+497 more', the screen stays truthful, but the group ordering in SGROUP_DEF now decides what the user sees first. Put OPPORTUNITY, WINDOW and PRODUCT before COMPETITOR.

Fixing events.name, news.outlet, news.url, science.date, researchers.org and channels.url changes fields that other domains are reading right now as empty. Anything currently rendering a fallback dash for those will start rendering content, and anything that branched on the null (a `hasX` flag) will flip.
